used on the feast of Imbolc

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Biddy is an Irish name for the goddess Brigit. People used it on the spring feast of Imbolc. Children then went begging from house to house. In Kerry, white-garbed young men were the Biddy Boys. They sang a short verse for the poor. The custom faded late in the twentieth century. It has since been revived in Kerry itself.

okr.objective: Biddy is a folk name for Brigit that survives in a custom and dance around the feast of Imbolc.
